t.3.12.1: Rāma, I am pleased; may good fortune be yours. I am delighted, Lakṣmaṇa, that you two have come together with Sītā to pay your respects to me.
t.3.12.2: Weariness from the toil of the road, a heavy fatigue, oppresses you two, and clearly Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, is also longing for rest.
t.3.12.3: For she is delicate and has never been humbled by hardships, yet, impelled by love for her husband, she has come to this forest so full of perils.
t.3.12.4: You, Rāma, must act so that Sītā here may be happy, for she has done a difficult thing in following you into the forest.
t.3.12.6: Women imitate the fickleness of lightning flashes, the sharpness of weapons, and the swiftness of Garuḍa and the wind.
t.3.12.5: This indeed has been the nature of women since creation, O Raghunandana: they cling to a man who stands in good fortune and abandon him who has fallen into adversity.
t.3.12.7: But this wife of yours is free from these faults; she is worthy of praise and worthy to be held up as an example, just like the goddess Arundhatī.
t.3.12.8: O Rāma, subduer of foes, this region where you will dwell together with Saumitri and with this Vaidehī will indeed be adorned.
t.3.12.9: Thus addressed by the sage, Rāghava, his hands joined in reverence, spoke these humble words to the seer, who blazed like a kindled fire.
t.3.12.10: Blessed am I, favored am I, since the bull among sages, the bestower of boons, is pleased with the virtues of me, together with my brother and my wife.
t.3.12.11: But point out to me a place with water and abundant forests, where, having made a hermitage, I may dwell happily, content and devoted.
t.3.12.12: Then, having heard Rāma's words and reflected for a moment, the best of sages, righteous-souled and steadfast, spoke words still more steadfast.
t.3.12.13: Two yojanas from here, dear son, lies a splendid region abounding in roots, fruits and water, full of many deer, renowned as Pañcavaṭī.
t.3.12.14: Go there and, together with Saumitri, make your hermitage; delight there, faithfully keeping your father's word just as it was spoken.
t.3.12.15: For this whole account of yours is known to me, O sinless one, both through the power of my austerity and through my affection for Daśaratha.
t.3.12.17: And therefore I tell you: go to Pañcavaṭī. For that is a delightful stretch of forest, and Maithilī will take pleasure there.
t.3.12.16: And by my austerity I have come to know the wish that dwells in your heart, having promised to make your dwelling here with me in this grove of penance.
t.3.12.18: That region is praiseworthy and not too far from here, O Rāghava. It lies near the Godāvarī, and Maithilī will be happy there.
t.3.12.19: It abounds in roots and fruits and is filled with flocks of many kinds of birds; it is secluded too, O mighty-armed one, and holy and delightful as well.
t.3.12.20: You, too, are accompanied by your wife and are capable of protecting; moreover, Rāma, dwelling here you will protect the ascetics.
t.3.12.21: O hero, this great forest of madhūka trees can be seen; one heading toward the banyan tree should pass along its northern side.
t.3.12.23: Thus addressed by Agastya, Rāma, together with Saumitri, honoured that truth-speaking sage and bade him farewell.
t.3.12.22: Then, after climbing onto the high ground not far from the mountain, there is a place known as Pañcavaṭī, whose woods are ever in bloom.
t.3.12.24: Then the two of them, given leave by him, having bowed at his feet, set out from that hermitage for Pañcavaṭī together with Sītā.
t.3.12.25: Then the two sons of the lord of men, bows in hand and quivers fastened on, never fainthearted in battles, set out with composed minds for Pañcavaṭī by the path the great sage had pointed out.
